issues: Label smoothing is on only when self.training is true. The val_bpb result is valid only if the model is in eval mode when it is evaluated. The standard train.py calls model.eval() before evaluate_bpb, and the harness recomputes val_bpb itself. If evaluation ever ran in training mode, the smoothed loss would make val_bpb look worse, not better, so this cannot be gamed in the candidate's favour.
No evaluation code, data, seed lines or eval call were changed. The edit only adds an argument to the training loss.

The training loss printed during the run now includes smoothing (about 0.05 times the cross-entropy against a uniform distribution), so it cannot be compared with the incumbent's training loss. Only the harness val_bpb counts.
Setting a training-mode flag inside the compiled forward can trigger a torch.compile recompile when the mode switches. That costs a little time but does not change the result.

In practice, label smoothing usually makes bits-per-byte worse for language models, because it trains the model to be less confident than the true distribution. Expect this run to come out neutral or worse.
